articles.title: Preview vs render
articles.summary: The live preview updates by itself and never writes files; RENDER builds the real paint and spec and copies them to your iRacing car folder. You only render when the look is right, then Alt+Tab to iRacing and press Ctrl+R.
articles.what: Two different things share the middle of the window. The LIVE PREVIEW redraws by itself after you change a zone, a colour or a finish, so you can judge the look. RENDER is the slow, full-quality step: it builds the finished paint file and the spec file (the shine map) and copies them where iRacing can load them. iRacing then lights your car with its own sun, shadows and materials and adds its own number and sponsor stamps, so the same colours and patterns show up but the shine is never an exact match for the preview.
when: You changed something and want to see it before spending a full render.
The preview looks stale, blank or stuck.
The car looks a little different in iRacing than in the preview.
how: Change a zone, colour, finish or slider. The LIVE PREVIEW (right of SOURCE) updates by itself after a moment.
If it did not change, press Refresh above the preview (or F5). Refresh stops a stuck preview and starts a new one.
After a render, click Compare to drag a divider between the source and the render and see what your change really did.

Use the chips above the preview (COMBINED, R METAL, G ROUGH, B COAT) to look at the shine itself: brighter red means more metal, darker green means a sharper mirror, blue closest to 16 (very dark, but not black) means the glassiest clearcoat, and black means none.
When the look is right, press RENDER. Only RENDER writes files; the preview never touches your iRacing folder.

A change to the spec (shine) only shows in iRacing after a render; the preview cannot reload the sim for you.

articles.title: The Render button and render size (2048 / 1024)
articles.summary: RENDER builds full paint/spec job outputs from the loaded source. Check the separate output-folder and Live Link statuses to confirm delivery; a preview or overall job-success status alone does not prove the car folder was updated.
articles.what: RENDER is the big button in the centre of the window (keyboard: Ctrl+R inside Shokker). It builds the paint file and the spec file for the whole car and attempts delivery to the iRacing car folder in the top bar, with a separate delivery status. The size is not a setting: Shokker renders at the size of the template you opened, and iRacing car paints are 2048 by 2048 (or 1024 by 1024). Always open the template for the car you drive and never resize the canvas.
when: Your preview looks right and you want it in iRacing.
You changed a zone and want to see it in the sim.
RENDER will not start and you need to know what is missing.
how: Open your car template with Open Paint...: Layered template for a layered paint or Flat image for a flat paint, and wait until the RENDER button switches on.
Type your iRacing User ID (Customer ID) and pick your car in iRacing Car Folder at the top.
Turn the template layers (Mask, Wire, Car_Mandatory) OFF in the Layers panel.
Press RENDER. A green Saved bar appears when the files are written.
Switch to iRacing and press Ctrl+R there to reload the car.

articles.title: Render history and keeping versions

You want to compare two looks.

Click a thumbnail: Shokker rebuilds that look completely. Press Gallery in the footer to see all past renders at a larger size.
Press Recent to pick from the last 10 saved renders with their recipes.
After a render, press Save to keep on the recipe card to copy that render into a keep folder.
To share the look, use Share Recipe (a .shokkerrecipe file with a preview) or Save Card PNG for a picture.

articles.summary: Full car renders produce named paint and spec files in a job folder; delivery to the selected car folder has a separate status. Check actual paths, customer ID and copy results before assuming iRacing has the new files.

deep.body: The paint is car_num_ID.tga (Custom Number) or car_ID.tga (Sim-Stamped Number). The shine is car_spec_ID.tga. The ID is your iRacing Customer ID, not your car number. The spec file is red = metal, green = roughness, blue = clearcoat and alpha = lighting mask.

deep.body: Paints are saved as 24-bit TGA, 2048 or 1024 square. Only cars with paintable glass need 32-bit with the template glass alpha filled. iRacing builds a .mip from the spec the first time it loads it.

deep.body: You may also see spec_*.tga, paint_base.tga and ORIGINAL_* backups of files Shokker replaced. They are harmless. Do not rename the main files: iRacing loads only files with your own ID in the name.

faq.a: No. It is your iRacing Customer ID.

faq.a: A backup of a file Shokker replaced. It is harmless.

faq.a: No. Only Shokker can.

faq.q: What bit depth does the paint use?
faq.a: 24-bit TGA.

faq.q: Can I copy the TGA into the iRacing folder myself?
faq.a: Yes. iRacing only cares about the file name and the folder: car_<ID>.tga (or car_num_<ID>.tga) and car_spec_<ID>.tga with your Customer ID, in Documents > iRacing > paint > the car folder. Setting the iRacing Car Folder makes Shokker copy them for you on every render, and Deploy Now sends the last render to a car.

faq.q: Where do I put the spec file?
faq.a: In the same car folder as the paint file. Shokker copies both there on every render; without car_spec_<ID>.tga the paint shows but with the default shine.

faq.q: What bit depth and colour mode should my TGA be?
faq.a: Use the files Shokker writes as they are: the paint is a plain 24-bit RGB TGA and the spec is 32-bit, because its alpha is the lighting mask. Re-saving the paint in another editor can add an alpha channel and show holes in iRacing.

faq.q: Why does the file need my number in the name? Can I call it MyPaint.tga?
faq.a: iRacing only loads files that carry your Customer ID in the name (car_ID.tga and car_spec_ID.tga), so a file called MyPaint.tga is ignored by the sim. It is a rule of iRacing, not Shokker; keep the names Shokker writes. The ID is your Customer ID, not your car number.

faq.q: Where does the spec file go, and is the paint file alone enough?
faq.a: Every render writes a paint file and a spec file (car_spec_ID.tga) into your iRacing car folder. The paint file alone gives the colour; the spec file is the shine, so keep both.

The top-bar Custom Number and Sim-Stamped Number choices select car_num_<CustomerID>.tga and car_<CustomerID>.tga respectively. They do not edit race-number pixels. faq.q: Where do I type my car number?
faq.a: Text (T) or Car > Number Kit accepts number artwork. These top-bar switches choose filenames; their Customer ID field is your account ID.

faq.q: Why do I see the number twice?
faq.a: Check baked-in source numbers, Number Kit’s Add Alongside/Replace Existing choice, and a simulator stamp over the artwork. A filename mode does not erase old number pixels.

faq.q: Does Shokker know the iRacing setting?
faq.a: No. It cannot read it. You have to look.

faq.q: Do I need to restart iRacing?
faq.a: Yes, after changing Hide Car Numbers.

faq.q: Why is there a car number file separate from the paint file?
faq.a: Plain explanation: car_num_ID.tga is the paint with your own number baked in, and car_ID.tga is the paint iRacing stamps a number on. The number modes decide which file iRacing uses, so the same car can give you either file.

faq.q: The numbers come from the sim. Can I remove or change them in Shokker?
faq.a: No paint tool can. iRacing stamps them on top when it loads car_<ID>.tga (Sim-Stamped Number). To control the number yourself, switch to Custom Number, set Hide Car Numbers ON in iRacing and put your own number on a layer (the Number Kit does this), or leave it out.

faq.q: When does the sim stamp the car numbers?
faq.a: Whenever iRacing loads the car_<ID>.tga file: Sim-Stamped Number mode with Hide Car Numbers OFF, which is the iRacing default. It then stamps the driver number and sponsors on top of your paint. With Custom Number and Hide Car Numbers ON it stamps no number.

protips: Custom Number paints need Trading Paints Pro for sharing. Sim-Stamped Number paints do not.

Inspect the job output directory and named paint/spec TGAs. Check the separate selected output-folder and Live Link/iRacing-copy status rather than assuming every product went to one place.
Verify the exact car folder, account Customer ID and Custom/Sim paint filename. Keep a first-write ORIGINAL_ backup separate from the current job output; it is not a history of every render.
An editable source PSD/project, paint TGA, material spec TGA, recipe and generated .mip have different purposes. Preserve source/project backups and use the actual output paths for file location.

deep.heading: Current source-qualified workflow
deep.body:
The selected output folder is the destination for a copy attempt after job rendering. Check output_dir and Live Link status/path; a successful job preview does not guarantee successful copying. Choose the actual existing folder for the intended car rather than assuming a remembered target matches it.

1. After a render, inspect the actual job result and Saved/error bar. Use Show my files when available; a reported path alone does not prove the current file was written.

faq.q: Can I upload the spec as a TGA?
faq.a: No. Trading Paints takes the spec only as a .mip.

faq.q: Where does the .mip come from?
faq.a: iRacing builds it from car_spec_ID.tga the first time it loads the car.

faq.q: Can I upload my project file?
faq.a: No. Upload the rendered TGA.

faq.q: Does Shokker upload for me?
faq.a: No. Copy TP Desc only copies a description.

faq.q: Does iRacing read the spec from the TGA or the MIP?
faq.a: On your own PC iRacing reads car_spec_ID.tga and compiles it into car_spec_ID.mip next to it; Trading Paints can only share that .mip. The spec is read as raw numbers with no colour correction, while the paint is read as normal screen colour. An old .mip can hide a new TGA until you press Ctrl+R in the sim or move the .mip out of the folder.

faq.q: Does the number mode change what I upload to Trading Paints?
faq.a: The paint file changes: Sim-Stamped Number writes car_ID.tga (a Sim-Stamped Number paint on Trading Paints) and Custom Number writes car_num_ID.tga (a Custom Number paint, which needs Trading Paints Pro). Upload the one that matches your mode. The spec is car_spec_ID either way, shared as the .mip.

faq.q: How do I stop Trading Paints from replacing my local paint?
faq.a: Close the Trading Paints Downloader, or turn off its Update My Own Paints option, while you test: it may overwrite the files in your car folder. Turn it back on when you are done. I do not know the exact menu name, so look in the Trading Paints app settings.

faq.q: Is very fine detail lost in the MIP?
faq.a: Distance fades it, not the file type: iRacing shows smaller, averaged copies of a texture as the car gets farther away, so single-pixel detail disappears first. Choose patterns and spec at car scale (the guide calls 4 to 8 px the fine band) and judge the result in the sim. This is separate from the .mip file Trading Paints uses for the spec.

faq.q: Does iRacing mip the spec map, and is very fine detail pointless?
faq.a: Distance fades fine detail, not the file type: iRacing shows smaller, averaged copies of a texture as the car gets farther away, so single-pixel detail disappears first. Choose patterns and spec at car scale (the guide calls 4 to 8 px the fine band) and judge the result in the sim. This is separate from the .mip file Trading Paints uses for the spec.

faq.q: Do I upload it to Trading Paints?
faq.a: Yes, if you want other drivers to see it, because iRacing never sends textures between drivers. What you upload depends on the number mode: Sim-Stamped Number writes car_ID.tga and Custom Number writes car_num_ID.tga (needs Trading Paints Pro). Shokker does not upload for you; the spec goes up as the .mip iRacing builds.

faq.q: Does the sim-stamped number change what I upload to Trading Paints?
faq.a: Yes: the number modes decide which paint file you make. Custom Number means the file has your own number (car_num_ID.tga, a Custom Number paint that needs Trading Paints Pro); Sim-Stamped Number writes car_ID.tga and iRacing stamps the number. Trading Paints uploads follow the files you make, and the spec goes up as the .mip.

faq.q: How do I get iRacing to use my local paint instead of the Trading Paints one?
faq.a: Trading Paints controls which files land in your folder: close the Trading Paints Downloader, or turn off its Update My Own Paints option, while you test, so it does not overwrite your local files. I do not know the exact menu name, so look in the Trading Paints settings, and turn it back on afterwards.

faq.q: How do I get iRacing not to use the TP paint for my own car and use my local one?
faq.a: Trading Paints controls that: pause or turn off TP for that car, for example close the Trading Paints Downloader or turn off its Update My Own Paints option while you test. I do not invent the exact menu name, so look in the Trading Paints settings, and turn it back on afterwards.

faq.q: I have both Trading Paints and my local Shokker paint, which one does the sim use?
faq.a: Whichever files are active in your car folder when the sim loads: the Trading Paints Downloader writes the same file names and may overwrite your local paint. Close it or turn off Update My Own Paints to test local files, and keep them in step by re-uploading after changes.

articles.summary: Photoshop round-trip produces composed paint/spec TGA exchange files and separate grayscale channel TGAs, not a reconstructed PSD layer stack. Verify actual file existence and freshness; a manifest alone can include missing primary paths or retained old channel files.

articles.title: Saving projects, recipes and reloading later
articles.summary: Save / Open keeps your editable project: zones, layer settings and available edited layer pixels. Keep its original source paint unchanged at the saved path. A rendered TGA is flattened output; recipes replace zones and do not restore editable layers.
articles.what: Save / Open opens SPB PROJECTS. SAVE CURRENT saves a .spbproj workflow, including zones, layer settings, available layer pixels and live text. It also records the source paint path and fingerprint. It does not replace a backup of the original PSD or guarantee that a project can open on another computer. Keep the original source unchanged and accessible at its saved path. Projects also retain Number Kit, Sponsor Kit, Car-Space Fade, Race Wear, Layer Materials, Colourway variants and Edge Bleed settings. A .shokkerrecipe carries zones, colours, finishes and effects; Import Recipe replaces current zones after confirmation. SAVE SHOKK can include the paint TGA for sharing a look, but that is not the original layered PSD. RENDER creates the output files for iRacing or Trading Paints. Ctrl+S refreshes local autosave, not a portable backup.

You want to send a look to a friend.
You want a backup before experimenting.

Come back later with Save / Open and load it. Check your iRacing User ID and car folder afterwards: loading someone else's file can overwrite them.

To use a shared look, press Import Recipe and choose the .shokkerrecipe file.

articles.title: Rendered TGA formats: paint, spec and channel order
articles.summary: The current car renderer sends paint to the 24-bit writer and RGBA spec to the 32-bit writer. On-disk BGR/BGRA ordering is handled by the writer, not by decorative recolouring.
articles.what: The current car renderer sends paint to the 24-bit writer and RGBA spec to the 32-bit writer. On-disk BGR/BGRA ordering is handled by the writer, not by decorative recolouring.
when: Checking an export file or diagnosing output that differs from the editor or simulator.
how: Check the actual source, filename and destination status for the operation used.
Validate file dimensions and contents separately from on-car appearance.
pitfalls: These facts describe inspected SPB paths, not every export path or simulator compatibility guarantee.

faq.q: Does the current SPB car renderer write 24-bit paint and 32-bit spec?
faq.a: Yes. The actual car output calls write_tga_24bit for paint_rgb and write_tga_32bit for combined_spec_u8. Some low-level docstrings describe these roles backwards; the call sites and written headers are the authority for this path.

faq.q: Should I swap red and blue material channels because a TGA stores BGRA?
faq.a: No. The writer converts logical RGBA to on-disk BGRA, or RGB to BGR, as a file encoding step. An ordinary decoder reverses that encoding. Manually exchanging logical material channels changes metal/roughness/coat semantics instead of repairing the file.

faq.q: What does the 32-bit TGA writer do if it receives only three RGB channels?
faq.a: It promotes an H by W by 3 array to four channels with alpha 255. This fallback supplies opaque alpha; it does not reconstruct an authored lighting mask that was missing from the input.

faq.q: Can the 24-bit paint writer preserve an alpha channel from RGBA artwork?
faq.a: No. The 24-bit writer trims extra channels to the first three. Keep the layered project or original RGBA asset for editable transparency; this flat paint output is not a transparency-preserving project backup.

faq.q: Does giving the TGA writer a PNG filename make it produce PNG bytes?
faq.a: No. These low-level writers emit TGA headers and pixel bytes regardless of the filename extension. Use the correct export path and extension rather than renaming a TGA and expecting another format.

articles.title: TGA writer limits: dimensions, numeric conversion and errors
articles.summary: The writer serializes the supplied array size and bytes. It does not resample a template, preserve fractional channel values, or raise every write failure to the caller.
articles.what: The writer serializes the supplied array size and bytes. It does not resample a template, preserve fractional channel values, or raise every write failure to the caller.
when: Checking an export file or diagnosing output that differs from the editor or simulator.
how: Check the actual source, filename and destination status for the operation used.
Validate file dimensions and contents separately from on-car appearance.
pitfalls: These facts describe inspected SPB paths, not every export path or simulator compatibility guarantee.

faq.q: Will the TGA writer automatically resize my paint to 2048 square?
faq.a: No. It writes width and height from the supplied array. The general source loader takes the loaded image dimensions; correct template/output dimensions must be established upstream. A successful write alone does not certify the dimensions are appropriate for the car.

faq.q: Does the TGA writer round fractional material values or preserve them?
faq.a: For non-uint8 arrays it clips to 0–255 then casts to uint8. Positive fractions are truncated by that cast: 100.9 becomes 100, while values below zero or above 255 clip to the endpoints. These are byte-conversion facts, not physical material calibration.

faq.q: Must I vertically flip the TGA because its rows are written top first?
faq.a: The writers mark top-left origin in the header: descriptor 0x20 for 24-bit and 0x28 for 32-bit with alpha bits. A compliant reader uses that orientation. Do not flip the artwork solely because you inspected the raw row order.

faq.q: Does a TGA writer returning normally guarantee a valid output file?
faq.a: No. These functions log invalid shapes, zero-area images and I/O failures and return without raising them. Check the actual file or higher-level delivery result; a normal Python return is not a successful-write receipt.

articles.title: Render products: previews, names and optional derived normals
articles.summary: Preview arrays, full-render TGAs and optional derived normals serve different purposes. Their existence does not prove current native appearance or calibrated surface geometry.
articles.what: Preview arrays, full-render TGAs and optional derived normals serve different purposes. Their existence does not prove current native appearance or calibrated surface geometry.
when: Checking an export file or diagnosing output that differs from the editor or simulator.
how: Check the actual source, filename and destination status for the operation used.
Validate file dimensions and contents separately from on-car appearance.
pitfalls: These facts describe inspected SPB paths, not every export path or simulator compatibility guarantee.

faq.q: Does an engine preview render save final paint and spec TGAs?
faq.a: The preview_mode branch returns the arrays before the final file-writing block. It skips those output TGAs and PNG saves. A live preview image is therefore not proof that this branch saved final files to the car folder.

faq.q: Does Custom Number mode change the spec filename as well as the paint filename?
faq.a: No. The current render chooses car_num_<CustomerID>.tga or car_<CustomerID>.tga for paint, while spec remains car_spec_<CustomerID>.tga. The suffix is the configured iRacing customer identifier, not a racing number or car-model identity.

faq.q: Are PREVIEW_paint.png and PREVIEW_spec.png editable project backups?
faq.a: No. This full-render path saves PNG images from the composed paint/spec arrays. They are flat visual/data outputs, not layers, masks, history or recipes sufficient to recover an editable project. They also do not establish native car appearance or UV calibration.

faq.q: Does the optional normal TGA prove SPB has measured the car surface geometry?
faq.a: No. In this engine branch, generate_normal_map derives gradients from the metallic channel using Sobel and writes an RGB normal-like image. That is a derived material-field product, not measured car geometry or proof that the simulator consumes that optional file.

articles.title: PNG channel export: source selection and partial results
articles.summary: Channel PNG export reads an existing spec source and writes grayscale channel images. It does not render current edits, and optional outputs can be absent even when the channel operation succeeds.
articles.what: Channel PNG export reads an existing spec source and writes grayscale channel images. It does not render current edits, and optional outputs can be absent even when the channel operation succeeds.
when: Checking an export file or diagnosing output that differs from the editor or simulator.
how: Check the actual source, filename and destination status for the operation used.
Validate file dimensions and contents separately from on-car appearance.
pitfalls: These facts describe inspected SPB paths, not every export path or simulator compatibility guarantee.

faq.q: Does PNG channel export always use the current open editor state?
faq.a: No. It can use a requested spec path or extracted SHOKK data, then falls back to _latest_render and recent job files when no usable spec path is found. It reads an existing file rather than rendering the current editor. Check the returned spec_source before trusting the provenance.

faq.q: Are exported metallic roughness coat and mask PNGs red green blue and orange pictures?
faq.a: No. This endpoint writes each channel as a grayscale L-mode PNG containing that channel byte. Those inspection files differ from tinted preview displays. Recombining them requires the correct logical channel slots, not treating their gray pixels as decorative paint.

faq.q: Does include_paint guarantee paint_base.png accompanies PNG channel export?
faq.a: No. include_paint defaults true, but paint is saved only when a paint path exists and its conversion succeeds. Supplying only a valid explicit spec_path does not itself discover a paired paint path. Inspect the returned paths rather than assuming an absent paint was exported.

faq.q: Can channel export succeed even if spec_full.png could not be saved?
faq.a: Yes. The optional full RGBA backup save has its own caught error, while channel writes continue. The response paths list is the receipt for outputs actually recorded. Do not assume ok:true guarantees every optional backup or paint file exists.

faq.q: Where does PNG channel export put files when its destination is relative or unavailable?
faq.a: A relative requested path resolves under the application output folder’s PS_Exports directory; an empty path uses PS_Exports. If creation of a requested directory fails, the endpoint may fall back to PS_Exports after checking the write guard again. Read the returned paths to locate the actual outputs.

articles.title: Render delivery: job success, copy verification and backups
articles.summary: A render job and delivery to a chosen car folder have separate statuses. Verified copy means matching file bytes, not accepted simulator appearance or recoverable project history.
articles.what: A render job and delivery to a chosen car folder have separate statuses. Verified copy means matching file bytes, not accepted simulator appearance or recoverable project history.
when: Checking an export file or diagnosing output that differs from the editor or simulator.
how: Check the actual source, filename and destination status for the operation used.
Validate file dimensions and contents separately from on-car appearance.
pitfalls: These facts describe inspected SPB paths, not every export path or simulator compatibility guarantee.

faq.q: Can SPB report render success while copying to my car folder failed?
faq.a: Yes. The render result has overall success:true and may separately include output_dir or live_link with success:false, an error or a suppressed write. Check those destination-specific statuses; the job’s preview/download output does not by itself prove the car folder was updated.

faq.q: Can I paste a full paint file path into the output folder field?
faq.a: The active render resolver accepts an existing directory, an existing file path, or an explicit .tga path whose parent exists, even if the TGA is not created yet. It rejects a missing folder instead of silently falling back to its parent, and rejects unbalanced wrapper quotes. Prefer the intended car folder and check the returned destination status.

faq.q: Does verified render delivery prove the material looks correct in iRacing?
faq.a: No. The copy path compares destination size and SHA-256 against the job source. It proves exact copied bytes for that file, not a correct customer ID/car folder, simulator reload, material suitability, UV placement or native appearance.

faq.q: Why can render copying fail when iRacing or an image viewer is using the TGA?
faq.a: The copy path retries I/O failures up to eight attempts and verifies bytes after copying. Its final permission-error hint asks you to close the sim/preview or viewer using the target TGA and render again. Read the delivery error rather than repeatedly changing the finish recipe.

faq.q: When Live Link is enabled does it always use a separate remembered car folder?
faq.a: Not necessarily. The render route resolves the Live Link target with the visible output folder supplied and documents a preference for that folder. Inspect the returned live_link path/source; enabling Live Link alone does not establish which car folder received this render.

faq.q: Is ORIGINAL_ in the car output folder a new backup of every render?
faq.a: No. Before overwriting an existing destination, this copy path attempts an ORIGINAL_<filename> backup only when no such backup exists. Backup failures are logged and copying can continue. It is a first-write file backup, not a history of every render or a layered project save.

faq.q: Why can the engine keep using an ORIGINAL_ source instead of my edited flat file?
faq.a: Outside preview_mode, this engine branch creates an ORIGINAL_<source filename> backup if absent and loads an existing one to avoid cumulatively processing old rendered output. This is engine-source behavior, not a promise about every UI input path. Establish which source is actually loaded; preserve original files and use the intended import workflow rather than blindly deleting backups.

aliases: Render delivery: job success, copy verification and backups

articles.title: Photoshop exchange input: current payload and validation
articles.summary: The Photoshop route invokes a full pipeline using supplied paint/zones and a valid imported map. It is a composed-output exchange, with explicit input validation and its own settings.
articles.what: The Photoshop route invokes a full pipeline using supplied paint/zones and a valid imported map. It is a composed-output exchange, with explicit input validation and its own settings.
when: Importing a material map or sending composed output for external editing.
how: Verify source, dimensions and the exact output path used.
Keep the editable project/original separately and compare actual material bytes when preservation matters.
pitfalls: Source/stub-route tests are not native rendering or complete pipeline acceptance.

faq.q: Can Photoshop exchange run without any source paint input?
faq.a: No. The endpoint requires paint_file or paint_image_base64. A missing input returns 400, and a missing file path returns 404 when no image payload is supplied. A car name or spec map alone is insufficient for this exchange route.

faq.q: Does Photoshop exchange accept empty zones just because an import path was typed?
faq.a: The early check allows empty zones when import_spec_map is truthy, but later it passes that map only if the path exists. A nonexistent string can pass the early gate and then become None; that is not proof of a valid imported-map export. Verify file existence and the final operation result.

faq.q: Does Photoshop exchange only copy the last old render?
faq.a: This endpoint calls engine.full_render_pipeline with the current submitted paint and converted zone payload. That differs from PNG channel export, which selects an existing spec file. It is not a guarantee that every unsent editor change is in the submitted payload.

faq.q: Which paint wins if Photoshop exchange receives both a file path and a base64 paint image?
faq.a: The image payload is written to the job’s paint_with_decals.png and replaces paint_file for the exchange input. The selected file path is therefore not necessarily the pixels rendered by this request. Check the submitted payload when diagnosing discrepancies.

faq.q: Does Photoshop exchange treat spatial and region masks as interchangeable duplicates?
faq.a: No. Masks are decoded against the source canvas shape. When a spatial_mask payload is decoded, the route removes region_mask from that zone. These are explicit coverage inputs, not a semantic understanding of panel names; mismatched payloads can be rejected.

faq.q: Does a nonexistent imported spec path produce an immediate import-not-found error in Photoshop exchange?
faq.a: This route normalizes a missing/nonexistent imported spec path to None before its pipeline call, rather than issuing a dedicated missing-import response. With otherwise valid zones, output can therefore be produced without that intended map. Confirm the source and inspect material data.

faq.q: Does Photoshop exchange include helmet suit wear and ZIP output like every other pipeline option?
faq.a: This route explicitly passes helmet and suit as None, wear_level=0, export_zip=False and dual_spec=False. Those settings describe this operation, not a universal restriction on every SPB path or a guarantee about downstream simulator support.

articles.title: Photoshop exchange outputs: names, channels and freshness
articles.summary: Named exchange TGAs and a manifest are flat products. Inspect file existence and freshness; a successful response or retained channel filename is not proof of a newly complete layered export.
articles.what: Named exchange TGAs and a manifest are flat products. Inspect file existence and freshness; a successful response or retained channel filename is not proof of a newly complete layered export.
when: Importing a material map or sending composed output for external editing.
how: Verify source, dimensions and the exact output path used.
Keep the editable project/original separately and compare actual material bytes when preservation matters.
pitfalls: Source/stub-route tests are not native rendering or complete pipeline acceptance.

faq.q: Does the Photoshop car file name have to be an iRacing Customer ID?
faq.a: No. The exchange name is sanitized: letters/numbers plus dot, underscore, hyphen and space are retained; other characters become underscores, with a default shokker_export name. It names a subfolder and exchange files, not automatically a simulator-valid customer filename.

faq.q: Are Photoshop exchange car_num_00000 files my real customer paint filenames?
faq.a: No. This route uses temporary iracing_id=00000 and car_prefix=car_num for job output, then copies to <name>.tga and <name> Spec.tga. These are exchange names; they must not be confused with final customer-ID deployment files.

faq.q: Are Photoshop separated channel TGAs RGBA files retaining all four material channels?
faq.a: No. Each separated channel is replicated into three RGB slots and sent through the 24-bit writer as a grayscale TGA. The mask channel file contains alpha values as grayscale RGB, not as its own transparency channel. The combined Spec TGA is a different product.

faq.q: Does a successful Photoshop exchange manifest prove both named paint and Spec TGAs were newly created?
faq.a: No. Copies are conditional on each source file existing, but the manifest records paint_path and spec_path regardless. A successful manifest/response alone is insufficient; check the actual files and their freshness, especially after a partial pipeline output.

faq.q: Can old channel TGAs remain listed after a partial Photoshop exchange?
faq.a: Yes. The named exchange directory is reused. Channel files are copied only when job sources exist, and channel_files is built from files currently existing in the destination. A retained older channel can be listed without being newly exported in this request.

faq.q: Does a channel-export failure necessarily abort Photoshop exchange?
faq.a: No. The channel-generation block catches errors and logs a warning, and later exchange copying/manifest work can continue. Inspect the channel files and generation status rather than assuming overall success proves every channel was refreshed.

faq.q: Does Photoshop round-trip export reconstruct my editable PSD layer stack?
faq.a: This route writes composed paint/spec TGAs, grayscale channel TGAs and metadata files. It does not write a PSD stack or an editable SPB project. Keep the original layered document and SPB project separately; these flat exchange files have a different purpose.
